clue.text: Stealing can be infectious

definitions.meaning: ... something means stealing it, as in ... what is not yours
a ... disease is a catching one, an old sense of the word

explanation.surface: A warning that theft may spread like a disease.
explanation.definitionFit: Both senses are standard: the act of seizing goods, and an archaic adjective for contagious.

clue.text: Cook puts hock into what caters for kids

indicators.note: to cook figures is to doctor them, so the letters that follow are rearranged

parts.note: taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: A chef adds German wine to a dish meant for children.
explanation.definitionFit: A school snack shop is a British institution that sells sweets and buns to pupils.

clue.text: Bamboo fencing

parts.note: reads like a garden fence of canes, but means the Japanese martial art of fencing with bamboo swords

explanation.definitionFit: The Japanese sword art is fought with split-bamboo practice swords, so it is literally fencing with bamboo.

clue.text: It identifies an old name

parts.note: the French word for born, placed before a married woman's maiden surname

explanation.definitionFit: The word is used to introduce someone's former, birth surname, especially a woman's before marriage.

clue.text: A daughter's choice, to be fostered

parts.note: D is the standard abbreviation for daughter in family trees
an option is a choice

explanation.surface: A girl decides for herself to go into foster care.
explanation.definitionFit: Taking a child legally into one's family is the formal counterpart of fostering.

clue.text: Judge was powerless after her distressing deceit

definitions.text: Judge was powerless after her distressing deceit

parts.words: Judge was powerless after her distressing deceit
parts.note: Samson, a judge of Israel in the Bible, lost his strength when a woman tricked him into revealing that his hair was its source

explanation.walkthrough: Samson is called a judge in the Book of Judges; the woman who had his hair cut is the one meant.
explanation.definitionFit: The biblical temptress betrayed Samson to the Philistines, leaving the judge without his strength.

clue.text: Fail examination and teachers —- better put hand to this!

parts.note: in old university slang to plough is to fail a candidate in an exam
a school's teachers are its staff

explanation.surface: A failed pupil and disappointed teachers are told to knuckle down.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Put one's hand to the plough' means to set to work; the definition plays on that idiom.
explanation.definitionFit: The handle of a plough is the part a ploughman grips, so it is what one puts a hand to.

clue.text: Inflexible journalist at fault is put right

parts.note: an iron will is an inflexible one
ED, short for editor, is the crossword's usual journalist
out can mean wrong or mistaken, as in 'your sums are out'

explanation.surface: A rigid reporter's error is corrected.
explanation.definitionFit: To smooth away problems is to settle or correct them, an idiom from pressing creases flat.

clue.text: It can get under your skin

definitions.text: It can get under your skin

parts.words: It can get under your skin
parts.note: suggests something that annoys, but literally means a sharp object that pierces the skin

explanation.definitionFit: A sewing or hypodermic point literally goes beneath the skin, and the verb also means to irritate.

clue.text: Superficial appearance making part of coven eerie

indicators.note: part of says the answer is a run of letters hidden inside the words that follow

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: A witches' gathering puts on a spooky show for appearances.
explanation.walkthrough: The draft put 'making' in the definition; it is a link word joining the definition to the wordplay.
explanation.definitionFit: A thin decorative surface layer, figuratively a false outward show hiding something else.

clue.text: Dismissal is to stagger swimmer

parts.note: a congé is a formal dismissal, from French
to reel is to stagger

explanation.surface: Being sacked makes someone totter.
explanation.definitionFit: This large sea fish is a swimmer in the crossword sense of any fish.

clue.text: Layer in air beginning to oppress the area

indicators.note: the beginning of a word is its opening letter, here of oppress

parts.note: a zone is an area

explanation.surface: Something hanging in the atmosphere starts to weigh on the district.
explanation.definitionFit: This form of oxygen forms a protective band high in the atmosphere.

clue.text: Make an appearance in the Standard following exhibition

indicators.note: following says the Standard comes after the exhibition

parts.note: a show is an exhibition
a standard is a flag

explanation.surface: A banner is hoisted after a public display.
explanation.definitionFit: The idiom means to put in a token appearance, to be seen somewhere briefly.

clue.text: Very pleased, having caught fish (salmon by ring salmon)

clue.text: Length of a letter stated

indicators.note: stated means the letter is given as it is spoken

parts.note: the twelfth letter of the alphabet

explanation.surface: A query about how long a letter should be.
explanation.definitionFit: An old English measure of cloth, about forty-five inches.

clue.text: Major change for church if needed

indicators.note: change tells you to rearrange the letters of the words around it

parts.note: taken as written
CE is the Church of England
taken as written

explanation.surface: A suggestion that the church might alter things where required.
explanation.definitionFit: A major is an army rank, so is an example of a commissioned officer.

clue.text: Floral shrub, fairy host in disguise

indicators.note: something in disguise has its look altered, so the letters are rearranged

parts.note: taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: A crowd of fairies hides among the flowering bushes.
explanation.definitionFit: A garden shrub known for bright yellow flowers in early spring.

clue.text: Heard to deride work in plant

indicators.note: heard signals that the letters come from how the words sound

parts.note: to hiss at a performer is to deride them; OP is short for opus, a work

explanation.surface: Someone is overheard mocking labour in a factory.
explanation.definitionFit: An aromatic herb of the mint family, used in medicine and mentioned in the Bible.

clue.text: Time involved in handicraft for Peacock's castle

indicators.note: involved in means the letter is wrapped up inside the craft word

parts.note: crochet is a needlecraft using a hook

explanation.surface: A craft project about time, made for a peacock living in a castle.
explanation.walkthrough: Thomas Love Peacock wrote the novel Crotchet Castle (1831); his castle is named by the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: The novelist's satirical book is titled after the castle bearing this name.

clue.text: Part of an air-cooling system, say, about to limit stream

indicators.note: to limit something is to bound it, so the stream sits between two letters

parts.note: EG, for example, is what 'say' means
a rill is a small stream

explanation.surface: Engineering talk about restricting a flow of air or water.
explanation.walkthrough: 'about' makes GE; 'say' looks like it marks the definition as an example, but it supplies letters.
explanation.definitionFit: A grating over a vent or radiator lets air through in a cooling system.

clue.text: Puckish girdle allowing no latitude

parts.note: Puck in A Midsummer Night's Dream promises to put a girdle round the earth; this one sits at zero degrees

explanation.walkthrough: 'No latitude' is a pun: no leeway, and literally latitude zero.
explanation.definitionFit: The great circle around the earth's middle is at zero degrees latitude.

clue.text: Line in stouter flannel

indicators.note: in places the line letter inside the word for stouter

parts.note: stouter means fatter

explanation.surface: A line about a plumper woollen cloth.
explanation.definitionFit: Flannel as a verb is British slang for buttering someone up with talk.

clue.text: Threadlike pastry, not quite firm

parts.note: filo is a paper-thin pastry

indicators.note: not quite means the word loses its last letter

parts.note: set means firm, as a set jelly

explanation.surface: Flaky dough that hasn't fully hardened.
explanation.definitionFit: A botanical term for something with a slender thread-shaped end.

clue.text: Vices causing severe pains

explanation.surface: Bad habits leading to agony.
explanation.definitionFit: A carpenter's clamp is a tool for holding work, and the plural also means painful muscle spasms.

clue.text: Beam of light may be electric

definitions.meaning: the electric ... is a flat fish that stuns prey

explanation.surface: A remark that a shaft of light might carry current.
explanation.definitionFit: A narrow shaft of light, and a flat fish whose electric variety gives shocks.

clue.text: Doubtful ale upset — bad service again

indicators.note: upset means overturned, so the letters are rearranged

parts.note: taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: A pub complaint: suspect beer spilled, and poor service once more.
explanation.definitionFit: In tennis, two faulty serves in a row lose the point.

clue.text: Club head coming off in toto

indicators.note: the head of a word is its first letter, which is removed

parts.note: a putter is a golf club

explanation.surface: A golf club breaks completely apart.
explanation.definitionFit: The adjective means complete or total, which the Latin phrase expresses.

clue.text: Sudanese leader had one million constituents

indicators.note: constituents are parts that may be rearranged into a whole

parts.note: taken as written
I is the Roman numeral for one

explanation.surface: A Sudanese politician who had a million voters.
explanation.walkthrough: Muhammad Ahmad, the Mahdi, led the Sudanese revolt that took Khartoum in 1885.
explanation.definitionFit: The title of the Islamic messianic leader who defeated Gordon at Khartoum.

clue.text: International in check suit

parts.note: a test is a check
to match is to suit

explanation.surface: A cloth pattern described in fashion terms.
explanation.definitionFit: A cricket or rugby game between national sides; such players are called internationals.

clue.text: Clean hair

explanation.definitionFit: Both a cleaning action with a sponge-headed tool and a shaggy head of hair.

clue.text: Bare king through gawping crowd?

indicators.note: through puts the king letter right inside the crowd

parts.note: people who gawp are starers
K is the chess abbreviation for king

explanation.surface: A naked monarch passes through gaping onlookers, like the emperor with no clothes.
explanation.definitionFit: British slang for stark naked, completely without clothes.

clue.text: Vivacity of one involved in light spar

indicators.note: involved in means the numeral goes inside the word for the spar

parts.note: a sprit is a light spar holding up a sail
I is the Roman numeral for one

explanation.surface: Someone animated taking part in some friendly boxing.
explanation.definitionFit: Liveliness or vigour, as in performing with great spirit.
